questions.question: What does `<!DOCTYPE html>` at the top of a page do?
options: It links the page to its stylesheet
It tells the browser to render in modern standards mode instead of quirks mode
It sets the language of the page to English
It makes the page load faster on mobile
questions.explanation: Without a doctype, browsers fall back to quirks mode and emulate old rendering bugs. The doctype opts into standards mode.

questions.question: Your page shows up completely unstyled. What is the most likely cause?
options: The <link rel="stylesheet"> href path is wrong or the CSS file was not saved
The browser does not support CSS
questions.explanation: The href is resolved relative to the HTML file. A typo there means the CSS never loads, which DevTools also reports in the Console.

questions.question: You change a colour in the DevTools Styles panel and then refresh the page. What happens?
options: The edit is lost, because DevTools changes are not written back to your file
The edit is saved into style.css automatically
The edit is saved into index.html as an inline style
The browser asks whether to keep the change
questions.explanation: DevTools edits live only in the current page. That makes it a safe place to experiment before copying values into your editor.

questions.question: Why does every page in this course include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`?
options: It allows the page to show the ₹ symbol
It is required for the page title to appear
It stops mobile browsers from rendering the page as a zoomed-out desktop-width layout
questions.explanation: Without it, phones lay the page out at about 980px wide and shrink it, making text tiny. Character encoding is handled by the charset meta, not the viewport meta.
